question: India was ranked what in the Global Hunger Index 2024?
solution:
The correct answer is __**105th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India's Ranking:** In the **Global Hunger Index (GHI) 2024**, India has been ranked **105th** out of 125 countries.
 
• **Global Hunger Index (GHI):** The GHI is an annual report published by **Concern Worldwide** and **Welthungerhilfe**, assessing hunger across the globe using multiple indicators.
 
• **Indicators Used:** The GHI uses four key indicators: **undernourishment, child wasting (low weight for height), child stunting (low height for age), and child mortality**.
 
• **India's Score:** India scored poorly on parameters such as **child wasting**, where it has one of the highest rates globally at approximately **18.7%**.
 
• **Comparison:** India’s ranking is lower compared to its neighbors such as **Bangladesh (81st), Nepal (69th), and Sri Lanka (60th)**, highlighting challenges in addressing hunger and malnutrition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Global Hunger Index Methodology:**

 
 
• The GHI combines four indicators to calculate a score on a 100-point scale, where **0 is the best score (no hunger) and 100 is the worst score**.
 
• The four indicators include: **undernourishment** (population lacking adequate caloric intake), **child wasting** (low weight for height), **child stunting** (low height for age), and **child mortality** (death rate of children under five).
 
 
 
• **India's Challenges:**
 
 
• India struggles with high levels of **child wasting**, driven by factors such as **poverty, lack of access to nutritious food, poor sanitation, and inadequate healthcare services**.
 
• The prevalence of **undernourishment** remains significant, affecting millions of people due to income disparities and insufficient food distribution systems.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Neighbors:**
 
 
• India’s ranking is worse than its South Asian neighbors such as **Sri Lanka, Nepal, and Bangladesh**, indicating scope for improvement in combating hunger.
 
• Countries like Sri Lanka have better scores due to stronger healthcare and nutritional programs.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives:**
 
 
• India has launched several programs like **Poshan Abhiyaan**, **Mid-Day Meal Scheme**, and **Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS)** to combat malnutrition and hunger.
 
• Despite these efforts, the implementation and outreach of these programs need further strengthening.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Hunger Trends:**

 
 
• Globally, hunger has worsened due to factors like **climate change, conflict, and economic disruptions**, including the **COVID-19 pandemic**.
 
• Regions like **Sub-Saharan Africa** and **South Asia** face the highest levels of hunger.
 
 
 
• **Poshan Abhiyaan:**
 
 
• India’s flagship program for nutrition, launched in **2018**, aims to reduce **stunting, undernutrition, anemia**, and low birth weight by **2022**.
 
• The program focuses on leveraging technology, spreading awareness, and improving service delivery.
 
 
 
• **UN Sustainable Development Goals:**
 
 
• The **United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 2** aims to achieve **“Zero Hunger”** by **2030**.
 
• India’s progress on SDG 2 is crucial to global efforts in reducing hunger and malnutrition.
